newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW-Putnam Advisory eyes Japan fund business.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Putnam Advisory eyes Japan fund business.

text.p: Putnam Advisory Company Inc, the Japanese subsidiary of Boston-based Putnam Investments, has received approval to manage investment trusts in Japan, but says it is still skeptical about business prospects.

Managing director Takehiko Watanabe said that despite the approval to become a management company, Putnam Advisory will continue to focus on offering investment advisory services in Japan and market its funds through Japanese securities houses.

"I still don't see enough business opportunities for us to become an investment trust management company, while we can benefit from being an investment advisor and selling our funds through Japanese securities houses," Watanabe told Reuters.
He said Putnam Advisory may consider a possible alliance or joint venture with Japanese investment trust management firms.
"It is possible that we will form an alliance or a joint venture in the future with Japanese trust management firms that are affiliated with banks or life insurers," Watanabe said.
He added: "It is most important for us to consider what the best channel is to bring Putnam's products to Japan."

Putnam Investments, the sixth-largest mutual fund manager in the United States with total assets of nearly $180 billion, launched a strategic alliance with Japan's top life insurer Nippon Life Insurance Co to manage Japanese pension fund assets earlier this month.
The two firms will develop financial products and exchange information about markets and asset-management methods.
Watanabe said that he hopes the tie-up with the giant Japanese life insurer will create more business opportunities in pension fund management.
Meanwhile, Putnam Advisory's seminars has introduced Japanese institutions who are gearing up for "Big Bang" financial reforms to investment trust sales via banks.
Industry sources say Putnam has developed closer ties with Japanese banks through such seminars, which could help the firm form alliances.

Watanabe said Putnam is already ahead of the game with about 40 percent of Putnam Investments' mutual funds sold at banks in the United States. In Japan, banks are not yet authorised to sell securities investment trusts.

"Japanese banks are a bit nervous ahead of forthcoming changes under 'Big Bang' reforms and some city banks and regional banks have already attended our seminars to learn about our programmes," he added.

On Friday, an advisory panel to Japan's finance minister unveiled a set of recommendations for the reforms, including one that banks should be able to sell securities investment trusts after necessary changes in the legal framework. Bills are expected to be prepared in time for the January 1998 parliamentary session.
The panel also recommended that investment trust management companies be allowed to sell securities investment trusts over the counter at banks sometime in 1997/98.
Putnam Investments opened its first overseas office in Tokyo in 1983 and has been providing investment advisory services in Japan since 1987.
